exposedTools.name: code.commit
exposedTools.description: Request a Git checkpoint of this active writable session’s assigned checkout. Read its current HEAD with local Git first. Supply that full expectedHead, a commit message and a stable requestId. The message has a fixed shape: a first line of at most 72 characters saying what changed, then a blank line and, only where there is more than one thing to say, up to ten bullet points (each a line beginning "- "), one per significant change, each short. No paragraphs, no restated task, no session or commit ids. The owning runner performs fixed Git operations; this does not publish central or submit a proposal. It commits what the checkout holds and stages, ignored paths aside; a new or changed file over 50 MiB fails the operation, so keep such data out of Git. Returns a durable operation. If queued or dispatched, inspect code.operation with the returned command.id. Reusing the same request with different input is refused. The runner also commits this checkout by itself every five minutes ("Checkpoint: …"), which moves HEAD: an expectedHead that only those checkpoints have moved past is taken as the newest of them, so the commit lands on top of them. An operation that failed with workspace_head_conflict means HEAD moved after you read it: read it again and commit under a new requestId.

exposedTools.name: code.merge
exposedTools.description: Start materializes the frozen merge in a clean checkout. Complete commits its resolution with the current checkpoint and frozen second parent. Supply expectedHead, message and a stable requestId; poll code.operation for the receipt. The message has a fixed shape: a first line of at most 72 characters saying what changed, then a blank line and, only where there is more than one thing to say, up to ten bullet points (each a line beginning "- "), one per significant change, each short. No paragraphs, no restated task, no session or commit ids.

nodes.label: Research
nodes.purpose: Coordinates the outer cycle with only State, Scope and Workflows required. Domain Events, Paper, Reflections, Tasks, Experiments, Artifacts and Code Work bind optionally. Digests read selected Tasks and Experiments directly, without Knowledge. After approved reflection, accepted code missing from main is integrated through an ordinary reviewed Git Task and Code Work publication; otherwise the cycle can finish. Removing an optional provider blocks only operations that need it, and a replaced provider cannot commit an in-flight result. Stored records and completed command receipts remain readable. Historical cycles that require the retired Consolidation workflow retain their records and report research_consolidation_retired at its handoff.

exposedTools.name: research.advance
exposedTools.description: Advance the current outer gate. New cycles wait for selected work to finish, including failure or abandonment; scientific review approvals remain required. After reflection approval, a project without Git can complete. When Code hosts the project, accepted code that main does not hold yet is handed to one consolidation task; the cycle waits for its acceptance and its publication to main, injects a successor task when main moved first, and completes once main holds it. retryIntegration: true injects a fresh task after one ended without acceptance. Creates the next child workflows atomically, preserving their identities on replay. When the approved reflection carries a structured plan that continues, the advance that completes the cycle requires nextWave: create opens the plan’s tasks, experiments and the next research cycle in the same transaction, under you; skip completes without them. A text change specification creates nothing. Reuse the same requestId and exact expectedRevision for an uncertain response.

exposedTools.name: research.create
exposedTools.description: Start an outer research cycle around selected existing workflow IDs. It coordinates project definition, research and reflection; after reflection approval, a project without Git can complete. When Code hosts the project, accepted code that main does not hold yet is integrated by one consolidation task and published to main, and the cycle completes once main holds it. Before a long hosted cycle, read code.read status for known publication blockers and tell the operator about any repository automation or canary setup it needs; research can proceed while publication waits, and only the operator can attest a canary. This preflight does not verify live GitHub rules. exposedTools.name: session.ask_owner
exposedTools.description: Assigned worker only: end this visit with a question for the owner, when the work cannot go on without their decision or an action only a person can take (an operator’s fix, access, budget) and no tool can settle it. Your session closes at once, without counting as a failed launch; the work waits, withheld from dispatch, until an answer is queued to your thread. An optional responder may investigate and answer on the owner’s behalf; otherwise the question goes to the owner. The work then comes back to you in this same conversation, and the answer is the queued message you read with session.messages and acknowledge. Stop after calling it. Ask one self-contained question that says what you need and the options you see; a visit that keeps no conversation cannot ask.

exposedTools.name: session.ask_thread
exposedTools.description: Ask any thread's agent a question (threadId, from session.threads or the Agents page), live, dormant or retired: whoever may write in the project. A short inquiry visit resumes that agent's saved conversation, with read-only tools and no lease on its work, answers, and stops; its reply arrives on the question's message in session.thread_messages, where its inquiry status says queued, running, answered, unanswered or expired. It never moves the work or changes the agent's conversation: the agent's next work visit resumes as it left off and is told of the exchange. One question at a time per thread (inquiry_busy); a thread that kept no conversation cannot be asked (inquiry_unkept). The visit has 10 minutes to be taken by a machine and 10 to answer, and a model-token budget charged to you. Reuse requestId after an uncertain response.

exposedTools.name: session.await_compute
exposedTools.description: Assigned worker only: end this visit to wait for Sandboxes jobs or workflows of this work that run for more than about 15 minutes, instead of sleeping or polling. Your session closes at once, uncounted, and they keep running. The work comes back to you in this conversation once all have ended or one fails (a workflow once its captures register), when someone messages your thread, or by the result’s until: after minutes, or 15 minutes before a machine they run on reaches its lease end, so you can renew it or move on. Commit first, and release machines that run none of them. Stop after calling it.

exposedTools.name: session.dispatch
exposedTools.description: Project admin only, never a leased worker. Turn automatic dispatch of ready work to machines on or off for the project, and choose with ownMachines whether it goes only to the project's own runners (true) or also to machines Fleet rents (false). Turning dispatch on or off also clears every failed-launch count, as the go-ahead for the whole project. Fleet's machines here act as, and are paid for by, the project's owner (its admin, billed in Settings → Members), whoever changed either.

exposedTools.name: session.find
exposedTools.description: Find the current and latest worker session for one workflow instanceId. Use its threadId as the destination for session.message, which its live visit or its next one reads; no current session means no worker is live right now.

exposedTools.name: session.halt
exposedTools.description: Project admin only, never a leased worker. Close one offered or active session with sessionId, or, without it, turn automatic dispatch off and close every one in the project. reason is recorded (default operator_halt). Answers how many were halted.

exposedTools.name: session.message
exposedTools.description: Queue a durable message for a worker by threadId (a stage's worker, from session.find or session.threads), which its live visit or, once its work comes back, its next visit reads. A thread whose work has ended takes a message only as an answer. A message answers every question its agent asked with session.ask_owner, and dispatch then offers the work again. It also ends a wait its agent started with session.await_compute, which brings that work back at once. This does not interrupt local computation or prove the worker has read it. A pending message refuses the worker's next Merv call, carrying the message, and every one after it until the worker acknowledges it, so put what you have to say in one message rather than several, send none only to ask for status, and ask for a reply only when you need one. Reuse requestId after an uncertain response.

exposedTools.name: session.message.ack
exposedTools.description: Assigned worker only: acknowledge one queued message after reading it. Include a short reply explaining what you will do or why you cannot apply it. The acknowledgement and its reply are durable and written once: the same requestId and reply return it again, and anything else for an acknowledged message is request_conflict, so this is no channel for later notes. It records receipt, not incorporation into submitted evidence. An inquiry visit answers its question with this reply, which ends the visit.

exposedTools.name: session.messages
exposedTools.description: Assigned worker only: read your queue, oldest first: the messages to your thread that await your acknowledgement, those sent to its earlier visits included, and, in a visit that did not continue the thread's conversation, the ones earlier visits acknowledged, with their replies; call it without sessionId. acknowledged counts the thread's acknowledged messages, which all: true lists in full. While a message waits, every other Merv call you make is refused with session_message_pending: acknowledge each with session.message.ack, whose reply may say what you will do. A person reads a thread's messages with session.thread_messages.

exposedTools.name: session.observe
exposedTools.description: Anyone who can read the project, never a leased worker: the Merv calls of one thread (session.threads), its newest 100 with in-flight ones first, each with its visit, tool, status, timing and payload-size token estimates, and totals over all of them. Metadata only: never arguments or results.

exposedTools.name: session.question.resolve
exposedTools.description: Bound question responder only: answer the exact worker question, or escalate it as needs_you with what you investigated and the decision still needed. Repaired work counts as answered. Investigation failure counts as needs_you. Answering queues your explanation and releases the question blocker; escalation leaves the worker blocked. Reuse requestId after an uncertain response. A question already answered by a person, or whose revision moved, cannot be resolved.

exposedTools.name: session.release_hold
exposedTools.description: Project admin only, never a leased worker. Let automatic dispatch offer a held target again, after its cause is fixed: resets the failed-attempt count of one instance revision (instanceId and expectedRevision from a dispatch_held item of session.stuck) and records the reason. Idempotent by requestId; the same requestId with different input is request_conflict. hold_not_found when nothing is counted against the target, hold_not_held when it is still being retried. To not run the work at all, end or revise the record instead: a hold names one revision.

exposedTools.name: session.stuck
exposedTools.description: Read everything in the project that stopped moving, and why. Never for a leased worker. Kinds: session_idle (an active session with no Merv tool call for idleNoticeSeconds; a runner heartbeat is not progress), dispatch_held (a target withheld from automatic dispatch after failed launches), dispatch_failing (failing but still retried; listed, not counted in total), work_blocked (work another plugin published a blocker for, such as a Code base that cannot be derived yet; it is never offered, and next names the recovery), work_waiting (work whose agent ended its visit to wait for its Sandboxes compute with session.await_compute; it comes back by itself, so it is listed, not counted in total), work_deferred (three machines in a row took this work and could not prepare its checkout, because the place its history lives was away, busy or full; nothing counts that, so it is offered again and again, and code names the cause), ready_quiet (a ready step no session has taken for quietReadySeconds since its last revision change, operator steps included), dispatch_disabled, no_live_runner and runner_refusing (a live runner refused the same way for refusalSeconds). Each item carries since, forSeconds, code, why and next. why and next are advice; the server enforces every guard where it commits. At most 200 items; counts cover all of them.

exposedTools.name: session.thread_messages
exposedTools.description: Anyone who may read the work item, never a leased worker: what passed between one thread (threadId, from session.threads) and the people over it, oldest first. messages holds the messages to the thread, with their acknowledgements and replies; questions holds what its agent asked its owner with session.ask_owner, and whether a message answered it.

exposedTools.name: session.threads
exposedTools.description: Anyone who may read the work item, never a leased worker: the threads of one workflow instanceId, the worker of each stage and role, oldest first. Each has its state, role and status (live, dormant or retired) and its visits, oldest first: each session’s status, when it was offered, started and ended, its outcome and close code (why), whether it launched or resumed the thread’s conversation, its harness and runner.

exposedTools.name: system.status
exposedTools.description: Read operational status. People and Pi receive project dispatch, Fleet allocations, exhausted unclaimed Fleet retry blockers and model-budget wait status, runners, sessions, caller-admissible waiting work and blockers, including unusable workspace drivers. A leased worker receives only its own authenticated session, its work item's lineage (its threads and their visits, with runners) and model-budget wait status.

exposedTools.name: usage.read
exposedTools.description: Read what closed sessions cost: for the project, or with instanceId for that workflow instance together with everything it depends on and fans out to. Set includeDependencies false for the one instance alone. Wall-clock is measured by Merv from activation to close. Tokens and model are self-reported by the launching machine and unverified; reportedSessions says how many sessions reported, and accounting states what Merv cannot know. budgets lists the budgets in force and which dimensions are exceeded. Merv prices no session in money: a Fleet-hosted worker's model use is bounded by its person's daily Fleet token limit (system.status modelBudget), so unpriced worker, model or review charges are no reason to ask the owner.

exposedTools.name: usage.set_budget
exposedTools.description: Project admin only, never a leased worker. Set a budget on the project, or with instanceId on that instance and its dependency closure. Give maxWallMinutes or maxTokens; null clears a dimension and an omitted one is kept. A reached budget only pauses automatic dispatch with reason budget_exceeded: nothing running is stopped and people can still begin work by hand. Raising or clearing it resumes dispatch. Setting the same values again changes nothing. Only wall-clock is measured by Merv; a token budget trusts unverified self-reports and is judged only while every session in its scope that was activated reported usage — otherwise it pauses automatic dispatch with reason usage_unavailable until the report arrives or that bound is cleared. An instance budget whose dependency closure is too large to walk cannot be judged either: it pauses every automatic offer with reason usage_unavailable until its bounds are cleared. A budget covers worker sessions only, never the charges of a remote job.

exposedTools.name: session.dispatch
exposedTools.description: Project admin only, never a leased worker. Turn automatic dispatch of ready work to machines on or off for the project, and choose with ownMachines whether it goes only to the project's own runners (true) or also to machines Fleet rents (false). Turning dispatch on or off also clears every failed-launch count, as the go-ahead for the whole project. Fleet's machines here act as, and are paid for by, the project's owner (its admin, billed in Settings → Members), whoever changed either.

exposedTools.name: session.find
exposedTools.description: Find the current and latest worker session for one workflow instanceId. Use its threadId as the destination for session.message, which its live visit or its next one reads; no current session means no worker is live right now.

exposedTools.name: session.halt
exposedTools.description: Project admin only, never a leased worker. Close one offered or active session with sessionId, or, without it, turn automatic dispatch off and close every one in the project. reason is recorded (default operator_halt). Answers how many were halted.

exposedTools.name: session.message
exposedTools.description: Queue a durable message for a worker by threadId (a stage's worker, from session.find or session.threads), which its live visit or, once its work comes back, its next visit reads. A thread whose work has ended takes a message only as an answer. A message answers every question its agent asked with session.ask_owner, and dispatch then offers the work again. It also ends a wait its agent started with session.await_compute, which brings that work back at once. This does not interrupt local computation or prove the worker has read it. A pending message refuses the worker's next Merv call, carrying the message, and every one after it until the worker acknowledges it, so put what you have to say in one message rather than several, send none only to ask for status, and ask for a reply only when you need one. Reuse requestId after an uncertain response.

exposedTools.name: session.message.ack
exposedTools.description: Assigned worker only: acknowledge one queued message after reading it. Include a short reply explaining what you will do or why you cannot apply it. The acknowledgement and its reply are durable and written once: the same requestId and reply return it again, and anything else for an acknowledged message is request_conflict, so this is no channel for later notes. It records receipt, not incorporation into submitted evidence. An inquiry visit answers its question with this reply, which ends the visit.

exposedTools.name: session.messages
exposedTools.description: Assigned worker only: read your queue, oldest first: the messages to your thread that await your acknowledgement, those sent to its earlier visits included, and, in a visit that did not continue the thread's conversation, the ones earlier visits acknowledged, with their replies; call it without sessionId. acknowledged counts the thread's acknowledged messages, which all: true lists in full. While a message waits, every other Merv call you make is refused with session_message_pending: acknowledge each with session.message.ack, whose reply may say what you will do. A person reads a thread's messages with session.thread_messages.

exposedTools.name: session.observe
exposedTools.description: Anyone who can read the project, never a leased worker: the Merv calls of one thread (session.threads), its newest 100 with in-flight ones first, each with its visit, tool, status, timing and payload-size token estimates, and totals over all of them. Metadata only: never arguments or results.

exposedTools.name: session.question.resolve
exposedTools.description: Bound question responder only: answer the exact worker question, or escalate it as needs_you with what you investigated and the decision still needed. Repaired work counts as answered. Investigation failure counts as needs_you. Answering queues your explanation and releases the question blocker; escalation leaves the worker blocked. Reuse requestId after an uncertain response. A question already answered by a person, or whose revision moved, cannot be resolved.

exposedTools.name: session.release_hold
exposedTools.description: Project admin only, never a leased worker. Let automatic dispatch offer a held target again, after its cause is fixed: resets the failed-attempt count of one instance revision (instanceId and expectedRevision from a dispatch_held item of session.stuck) and records the reason. Idempotent by requestId; the same requestId with different input is request_conflict. hold_not_found when nothing is counted against the target, hold_not_held when it is still being retried. To not run the work at all, end or revise the record instead: a hold names one revision.

exposedTools.name: session.stuck
exposedTools.description: Read everything in the project that stopped moving, and why. Never for a leased worker. Kinds: session_idle (an active session with no Merv tool call for idleNoticeSeconds; a runner heartbeat is not progress), dispatch_held (a target withheld from automatic dispatch after failed launches), dispatch_failing (failing but still retried; listed, not counted in total), work_blocked (work another plugin published a blocker for, such as a Code base that cannot be derived yet; it is never offered, and next names the recovery), work_waiting (work whose agent ended its visit to wait for its Sandboxes compute with session.await_compute; it comes back by itself, so it is listed, not counted in total), work_deferred (three machines in a row took this work and could not prepare its checkout, because the place its history lives was away, busy or full; nothing counts that, so it is offered again and again, and code names the cause), ready_quiet (a ready step no session has taken for quietReadySeconds since its last revision change, operator steps included), dispatch_disabled, no_live_runner and runner_refusing (a live runner refused the same way for refusalSeconds). Each item carries since, forSeconds, code, why and next. why and next are advice; the server enforces every guard where it commits. At most 200 items; counts cover all of them.

exposedTools.name: session.thread_messages
exposedTools.description: Anyone who may read the work item, never a leased worker: what passed between one thread (threadId, from session.threads) and the people over it, oldest first. messages holds the messages to the thread, with their acknowledgements and replies; questions holds what its agent asked its owner with session.ask_owner, and whether a message answered it.

exposedTools.name: session.threads
exposedTools.description: Anyone who may read the work item, never a leased worker: the threads of one workflow instanceId, the worker of each stage and role, oldest first. Each has its state, role and status (live, dormant or retired) and its visits, oldest first: each session’s status, when it was offered, started and ended, its outcome and close code (why), whether it launched or resumed the thread’s conversation, its harness and runner.

exposedTools.name: system.status
exposedTools.description: Read operational status. People and Pi receive project dispatch, Fleet allocations, exhausted unclaimed Fleet retry blockers and model-budget wait status, runners, sessions, caller-admissible waiting work and blockers, including unusable workspace drivers. A leased worker receives only its own authenticated session, its work item's lineage (its threads and their visits, with runners) and model-budget wait status.

exposedTools.name: usage.read
exposedTools.description: Read what closed sessions cost: for the project, or with instanceId for that workflow instance together with everything it depends on and fans out to. Set includeDependencies false for the one instance alone. Wall-clock is measured by Merv from activation to close. Tokens and model are self-reported by the launching machine and unverified; reportedSessions says how many sessions reported, and accounting states what Merv cannot know. budgets lists the budgets in force and which dimensions are exceeded. Merv prices no session in money: a Fleet-hosted worker's model use is bounded by its person's daily Fleet token limit (system.status modelBudget), so unpriced worker, model or review charges are no reason to ask the owner.

exposedTools.name: usage.set_budget
exposedTools.description: Project admin only, never a leased worker. Set a budget on the project, or with instanceId on that instance and its dependency closure. Give maxWallMinutes or maxTokens; null clears a dimension and an omitted one is kept. A reached budget only pauses automatic dispatch with reason budget_exceeded: nothing running is stopped and people can still begin work by hand. Raising or clearing it resumes dispatch. Setting the same values again changes nothing. Only wall-clock is measured by Merv; a token budget trusts unverified self-reports and is judged only while every session in its scope that was activated reported usage — otherwise it pauses automatic dispatch with reason usage_unavailable until the report arrives or that bound is cleared. An instance budget whose dependency closure is too large to walk cannot be judged either: it pauses every automatic offer with reason usage_unavailable until its bounds are cleared. A budget covers worker sessions only, never the charges of a remote job.

exposedTools.name: workflow.extend_limit
exposedTools.description: Allow one workflow instance more rounds of a loop limit it has exhausted (gate loop_limit_reached). Project admins only, never a leased worker. The grant is recorded and adds to earlier grants; the instance keeps its state and revision. Each additional return allows one more pass through the capped loop. additional 0 adds no round and only resumes work suspended before its rounds were used up.

exposedTools.name: workflow.process
exposedTools.description: Read one instance's process graph, derived on read: the pinned definition's states and edges, which edges the record shows were actually taken and by whom, the live status and blockers of the current state's outgoing edges, and dependency edges to other instances. An edge means the machinery stepped through a gate; it never says a finding is correct. Per-record detail stays with the domain read.

exposedTools.name: workflow.status_and_next

With instanceId (the id of the work item, which is its workflow instance id), read the current gate, caller-specific next action, blockers, references and revision. limits reports each loop limit of the work with the state it leaves (from), so the review rounds used and remaining at each gate; at gate loop_limit_reached every allowed return there is used, nothing more is dispatched, and the work escalates to the project’s owner, who may decide it by hand or allow another round. Omit instanceId for a project overview of all workflow instances, where such work is listed under escalated. Optionally preflight an action (a name from actions[].action, never a tool name) with proposed input; this never executes it or reserves permission, and the answer’s preflight says which tool takes it. Commands recheck current rules. Use stable requestId values when calling mutation tools.
